title: Positive cohomology of a dense-open complement after open restriction
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, f:X -> Spec k a separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], U a dense open of X [def-weil-open-immersion], and i:Z -> X a closed immersion with image X minus U [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For any commutative coefficient ring Lambda and Lambda-module etale sheaf G on Z [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], every open immersion a:W -> X satisfies H^q(W,a^{-1}(forget(i_*G)))=0 for all q>0, where direct image, inverse image and cohomology are [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Neither G nor its stalks need to be torsion or constructible.

proof.text: X is Noetherian by finite type over k. Density of the open U places all generic points of the finitely many irreducible components in U. If the closed complement contained a strict specialization chain of length one, a generic point of X generalizing its upper point would lie outside the complement and extend the chain to length two, contradicting dim X <= 1. The complement is therefore zero-dimensional. The closed immersion i identifies Z topologically with this complement. Z is finite type over k and Noetherian; its finitely many irreducible components are single closed points. Their residue fields are k.

Form the pullback Z_W = W times_X Z. Its projection to Z is an open immersion, so it is an open subset of a finite zero-dimensional space. It is again separated finite type over k and zero-dimensional. The other projection i_W is a closed immersion, hence finite. Finite direct image commutes with pullback by the finite-exchange theorem. Forgetting module structure commutes with direct image sectionwise, and the module-pullback/forget natural isomorphism identifies the displayed object with i_W,* of the underlying abelian sheaf G restricted to Z_W.

Finite direct image does not change cohomology, by the bijective finite edge map. Positive cohomology on the zero-dimensional finite-type scheme Z_W vanishes. Equivalently, reduction is a finite union of spectra of the algebraically closed field k and its etale site has exact global sections. Transport the resulting Subsingleton instance across the comparison bijection in each positive degree. This includes empty Z_W and arbitrary module coefficients, with no torsion or constructibility assumption.
